% References to labels of another document with xr-hyper, from an .aux
% that LaTeX wrote under hyperref, with no .xref beside it. Each prints
% its number, page, or name as in the PDF, as does a label from an .aux
% that LaTeX wrote without hyperref. A label of this document still links
% to its heading.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{xr-hyper}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\externaldocument[X-]{test-xr/latex}
\externaldocument[P-]{test-xr/plain}
\begin{document}
Starred \ref*{X-s}. Section \ref{X-ss}. Page \pageref{X-front}.
Item \ref{X-item}. Bold \ref{X-emph}. Empty [\ref{X-none}].
Named \nameref{X-thm}. Named in italics \nameref{X-emph}.
Spaced \ref{X-step}. Included \ref{X-c}.

Without hyperref: subsection \ref{P-ss}, page \pageref{P-front}.

\section{Here}\label{here}
Local \ref{here}.
\end{document}
